title: Sammaan Capital Ltd - 535789 - Transcript Of Conference Call -Financial Results For The Quarter And Financial Year Ended March 31, 2026

summary.headline: Sammaan Capital's IHC takeover closed 31 March 2026; all three domestic agencies upgraded within 50 days, lifting bonds ~100 bps and targeting FY27 PAT of INR1,400 crore.
summary.overview: This was the first earnings call after IHC's strategic investment, with IHC's share allotment completed on 31 March 2026 and IHC holding 28.5% equity (43.5% after warrant conversion within 18 months). Management said INR5,652 crore (USD 592 million) has been received via equity and 25% warrant upfront, with about INR3,200 crore (USD 335 million) due on warrant conversion. CRISIL (9 April), CARE (12 May) and ICRA (23 May) upgraded the company to AA+ across all three, with CRISIL and ICRA up one notch and CARE up two. The call centred on a multi-year plan (FY27 to FY30) with a 4.4% steady-state ROA, cost-to-income falling to about 26%, and a shift to a co-lending and asset-light model, alongside a legacy-book write-off/credit cost discussion. The call also included a correction of the FY30 ROA figure from 8-odd percent to 4.4%.

segments.name: Residential mortgages (prime and affordable)
segments.commentary: Prime mass-market home loans (8.5% to 10% yield) to be sourced for sale to banks; affordable portion (10% to 13%) to be held on balance sheet. Management says mortgages drive growth in FY27 and FY28.

segments.name: Business loans and micro-LAP
segments.commentary: Prime mass-market loans yield 9.5% to 11% and are to be sold; semi-urban and micro-LAP loans yield 11% to 13.5% and are to be held.

segments.name: CRE project loans
segments.commentary: Done only on a co-origination basis with credit funds, pari-passu with no credit guarantee, with the company taking roughly 10% to 15% of disbursements.

segments.name: Gold loans and loans against securities
segments.commentary: Planned as the next secured products; gold needs a separate branch network, with wider product launches from FY28. About 240 branches are already sized for other products.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursements of about INR30,000 crore; Q1 FY27 disbursements to be at least 50% to 60% above Q4 FY26, then a 30% to 40% step-up on that base.

Marginal cost of funds to fall about 160 bps; cost of funds to decline 150 bps over three years; 270 bps total reduction tied to AA to AAA migration (120 to 150 bps on AA to AA+, and the rest on AA+ to AAA).
Portfolio mix target: 60% secured and 20% unsecured or semi-secured, with 80% retail; about 30% of incremental disbursements through co-lending or direct assignment.
Gearing capped at about 3.5x to 4x; liquidity held at the higher of 6 months of repayments or 10% to 15% of borrowings.
Target AUM of INR2 lakh crore and high-teen ROE (about 18%), with the timeline described as 'in no hurry'; FY27 and FY28 growth to be mainly mortgages.
capex_capacity: Branch network to grow fivefold to about 1,600 branches; workforce to rise to 20,000 people, with about 8,000 by end of FY26 per management.
A gold loan branch costs about INR20 lakh to set up and takes about 3 years to become fully productive and profitable; investment is not described as running into tens or hundreds of crore.
Technology spend (CRM upgrade and Salesforce deployment about 6 months ago) is expensed through the P&L, not capitalised; 37 AI use cases identified.
Targets: agent productivity up 30%, mortgage turnaround from 5 to 7 days to 2 to 3 days, loans per person per month from 0.6 to 2-plus.
demand_pricing: Management says productivity rose 2x between March and April 2026 following the shift to an asset-light model.
Disbursals of about INR72,000 crore planned for FY29 versus INR50,000 crore in CY17 and CY18 (as cited by management).
Competition: management says there are few AAA-rated NBFCs and that the market has room for new entrants; it cites AAA players (and 3 to 4 other AA+ players) disbursing around INR50,000 crore a year.
Management says insurance cross-sell reaches over 90% of borrowers.
Management says about 90% of borrowings are onshore; domestic bonds have appreciated about 100 bps since the IHC announcement, with international bonds about 250 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Varun Ahuja (BlackRock): Will offshore rating agencies follow the onshore upgrades, and is the slow cost-of-funds decline due to non-call fixed-maturity debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects international agencies to follow the domestic upgrades. Bonds cannot be renegotiated and have 3 to 4 year maturities, so the cost decline comes with a lag; incremental borrowing at lower cost and bank renegotiation are the levers.

qa_highlights.question: Renish (ICICI Bank): How will the company build non-mortgage portfolios, who will run them, and how will costs be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it has run secured and unsecured products at scale before, that tech and app-based lending help, and that people and tech investment will be made. Growth in FY27 and FY28 will be mainly mortgages, given no rush to hyper-grow.

qa_highlights.question: Bhanu Chauhan (Barclays): What share of growth comes from core versus new products?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 and FY28 disbursals are 80% existing products, falling over time; by FY30 the mix is targeted at 50% mortgage-backed and 50% other products.

qa_highlights.question: Avinash Singh (Emkay): How will competition from AAA NBFCs be handled, and is the FY30 ROA of about 8% correct?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the FY30 ROA figure was an error and corrected it to 4.4%, with FY27 at 1.8%, FY28 at 3.7% and FY29 at 4.4%. It says the market is large enough and that mortgage front-loading and co-lending support productivity.

qa_highlights.question: Naintara Ghosh (Deutsche Bank): How much investment is needed for the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment is mainly branches and people rather than large capex; technology costs already incurred (CRM, Salesforce) run through the P&L, and product-level ROA can be shared on request.

qa_highlights.question: Vineet Sharma (Param Capital): What drives the NIM rise from 3.5% to 5.8% when cost of funds is not falling as fast?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the NIM gain comes from the spread on sold-down loans (AUM less loan book rising from about INR30,000 crore to INR45,000 crore in FY28), and that equity adds liquidity without a P&L cost. Cost of funds shown is for on-balance-sheet borrowings only.

qa_highlights.question: Arun Antony (JM Financial): Is the 270 bps cost-of-funds reduction for FY27 still achievable given the West Asia conflict and rising yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 270 bps, with 120 to 150 bps coming from AA to AA+ and the rest from AA+ to AAA, and said the company is operationally, financially and promoter-ready for AAA.

qa_highlights.question: AS Raju (individual investor): What is the outstanding write-off as of 31 March, and will recoveries be included in projections?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said recoveries of about INR7,000 crore from amounts provided are built into the projections and described the provisions as credit costs, not write-offs. It said asset reconstruction company sales recover 70% to 80%.

risks_watch: Execution on FY27 disbursals (INR30,000 crore) and Q1 FY27 step-up; management's productivity claims rely on a 2x jump in one month.
Cost-of-funds path: 270 bps depends on AA to AAA migration; international agency ratings are still pending, and about 90% of borrowings are onshore.
Warrant balance of about INR3,200 crore (USD 335 million) due within 18 months, plus IHC's rise to 43.5%.
Credit-cost and recovery assumptions: the legacy book had provisions, with recoveries of about INR7,000 crore assumed; the call did not give a detailed write-off schedule.
Cost-to-income falling from ~50% to ~26% while hiring and building new products, with a risk of cost overrun during the transition.
A FY30 ROA projection error was corrected on the call; the revised presentation should be checked for other inconsistencies.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on ratings, cost of funds and the IHC relationship, with management stating it is 'in no hurry' on growth. It was more cautious on timing, saying the 270 bps cost-of-funds reduction depends on the AA to AAA path. It was evasive on some specifics, such as the write-off quantum, and it corrected the FY30 ROA figure during Q&A.
key_quotes: The chapter of the legacy book or the book itself stands firmly closed once and for all.
Each of those would eventually result in the profit targets being met.
AA+ is just the first stop. AAA is the destination.
I would refrain from calling this write-off. These are credit costs, which will enable management to focus on bandwidth.
